title: Sorting and Ordering Collections
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of sorting and ordering collections and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—comparable—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study sorting and ordering collections with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you select data structures according to ordering, uniqueness, lookup, and update needs. In this lesson, focus on comparable and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Choose a collection by its contract: ordering, uniqueness, key lookup, insertion/removal cost, and iterator behavior. Do not assume every implementation preserves order or supports concurrent mutation. Apply that reasoning specifically to comparable and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect comparable with comparator before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Comparator
items.text: Choose a collection according to ordering, uniqueness, lookup, and update requirements. Review equals/hashCode contracts, iteration behavior, and concurrent-modification rules before selecting an implementation.

items.title: Custom sorting rules
items.text: Arrays are fixed-length indexed containers. Check index bounds, iterate from the correct starting point, and choose a suitable search or sorting algorithm for the data and its existing order.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
